description.ncbi_summary: Sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca(2+)-ATPases are transmembrane proteins that catalyze the ATP-dependent transport of Ca(2+) from the cytosol into the lumen of the sarcoplasmic reticulum in muscle cells. This gene encodes a small proteolipid that regulates several sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca(2+)-ATPases. The transmembrane protein interacts with Ca(2+)-ATPases and reduces the accumulation of Ca(2+) in the sarcoplasmic reticulum without affecting the rate of ATP hydrolysis. [provided by RefSeq, Jul 2008].

uniprot_function.text: Reversibly inhibits the activity of ATP2A1/SERCA1 and ATP2A2/SERCA2 in sarcoplasmic reticulum by decreasing the apparent affinity of the ATPase for Ca(2+) (PubMed:11781085, PubMed:9575189). Also inhibits the activity of ATP2A3/SERCA3 (By similarity). Modulates calcium re-uptake during muscle relaxation and plays an important role in calcium homeostasis in muscle. Required for muscle-based, non-shivering thermogenesis (By similarity).
